summary: Verified the cjm-and-fixes-2026-08 package. Backend fixes 1 & 2 (analysis_cache wider unique index + cache-write wrapped in try/except) work end-to-end: DB shows only `study_method_filter_unique` on (study_id, method, filter_sig), the old `study_id_1_method_1` is gone, 5 MNL rows for study 6099… coexist for different filter slices, three filter query strings all return 200, cache reads hit on second identical call. The 161-test backend regression suite passes (36+22+31+49+23). Fix 3 primary defect — dropdown opening UNDER page content — is RESOLVED on all 5 requested pages (menu computed z-index=100, elementFromPoint returns a menu <a> itself → the dropdown paints ABOVE the content, and clicking a menu item successfully navigates). Regression modals still open above viewport. HOWEVER Fix 3 has a partial regression: the topbar's *sticky* behaviour is STILL broken on every .be-root page even though the CSS declaration is now `position: sticky; z-index: 40`. Root cause: `.be-root` carries `overflow: hidden auto`, which makes it the sticky element's scrolling ancestor; because .be-root's scrollHeight equals its clientHeight, the actual scroll happens on the window and the topbar scrolls off with the page. The CSS restore of specificity is correct, but the topbar is not sticky in practice.

ui_bugs.issue: Topbar computed style is position:sticky/z-index:40/top:0, but it does NOT remain visible when the user scrolls. After window.scrollTo(0,800) the topbar's getBoundingClientRect().top is -800 (or -518 on shorter pages) on every one of the 5 audited pages (/market-research/conjoint-analysis, /conjoint/results/6099…, /research/conjoint/6099…/design, /brand-equity, /brand-equity/studies/demo-sim-chathai-001). Root cause: .be-root has `overflow: hidden auto` which creates a scroll container but .be-root itself never scrolls (scrollHeight == clientHeight); the sticky element sticks to its non-scrolling ancestor while the window scrolls, so the topbar scrolls out of view. Suggested fix options: (a) remove `overflow: hidden auto` from .be-root (change to `overflow-x: clip` if you only need to kill horizontal overflow), or (b) hoist the topbar out of .be-root so it's a sibling, or (c) switch the topbar to position: fixed with a matching top offset on children.

action_items: Address topbar sticky regression: .be-root { overflow: hidden auto } silently prevents position:sticky from working when the window is the actual scroller. The blanket rule that pinned children at z-index 1 is now fine (dropdown appears above content — confirmed), but sticky itself is still not observable. Removing the auto overflow (or making .be-root itself the scrolling container with a fixed height) is the standard fix.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix 3 CSS restores position:sticky/z-index:40 on .be-root > .utb-root, but does not remove the underlying .be-root { overflow: hidden auto } that historically caused sticky to fail. The two changes must go together; otherwise users still don't get a sticky topbar.

rca_of_the_issue: position:sticky sticks to the nearest scrolling ancestor. When .be-root has `overflow: auto` (or `hidden auto`), it becomes that ancestor. In this app .be-root's clientHeight == scrollHeight (content fits its intrinsic height), so .be-root never scrolls; the window scrolls instead. Sticky then keeps the topbar pinned to .be-root's top, and as .be-root itself scrolls up with the window the topbar scrolls off screen. Fixing this requires removing the `auto` overflow from .be-root, or making .be-root the actual scroll container (fixed height + real overflow-y:auto), or hoisting the topbar out of .be-root.
